hotspots.title: Backlash mounts over executive order renaming Lake Ontario
hotspots.blurb: President Trump's executive order to rename Lake Ontario to 'Lake America' continues to spark outrage and mockery, with tech giants like Google and Apple considering compliance. The move is framed as a symbolic overreach amid broader tensions with Canada.
hotspots.affect: The renaming is a polarizing act of symbolic politics, provoking ridicule, nationalist pride, and cross-border diplomatic friction.

hotspots.title: Trump claims historic deal taking control of Venezuelan oil
hotspots.blurb: The Trump administration's oil deal with Venezuela, touted as the 'biggest in world history,' faces skepticism over its impact on gas prices and geopolitical implications. Critics and supporters clash over its feasibility and motives.
hotspots.affect: The deal is framed as a triumphant economic coup by supporters and a dubious, self-serving maneuver by critics, fueling intense debate.

hotspots.title: Outrage grows over aggressive immigration enforcement and deportations
hotspots.blurb: The Trump administration's immigration crackdown, including ICE arrests at bus stops and deportations of Afghans who aided U.S. forces, draws sharp condemnation. Supporters praise the enforcement as necessary, while critics decry it as cruel and unjust.
hotspots.affect: The enforcement actions are highly charged, with moral outrage from critics and defiant justification from supporters, amplifying existing divisions.

hotspots.title: JD Vance faces scrutiny over Israel stance ahead of RJC address
hotspots.blurb: Vice President JD Vance is under fire from Jewish conservatives over his past remarks on Israel and associations with figures like Tucker Carlson. His upcoming address to the Republican Jewish Coalition is framed as a test of his loyalty and leadership.
hotspots.affect: The controversy taps into intra-party tensions over antisemitism, Israel policy, and Vance's fitness for leadership, driving intense debate.

hotspots.title: Trump’s new tariffs on Canada spark legal and diplomatic backlash
hotspots.blurb: The Trump administration's 50% tariffs on Canadian goods, imposed under an untested law, strain U.S.-Canada relations and raise legal questions. Critics call it economic sabotage, while supporters see it as protecting American industry.
hotspots.affect: The tariffs are a flashpoint for trade wars, legal uncertainty, and nationalist economic framing, provoking strong reactions on both sides.
